Ivy: Heads-up: onboarding a new engineer hit a flurry of TS/ESM edge problems in our sample app. Main pain points: overloads losing inference, discriminated unions for tool outputs not narrowing, and Vite/esbuild resolving the wrong entrypoint.
Noah: can you paste the failing snippet + tsconfig? Vite's resolver sometimes picks the CJS export unless you set package.exports properly.
Ivy: repro is small: 
```ts
// call.ts
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'
const c = createClient()
const out = await c.tool<{ kind: 'rows'; rows: number }>('run')
if (out.kind === 'rows') console.log(out.rows)
```
TS complains `Property 'kind' does not exist on type 'unknown'` even though signature has overloads. tsconfig: { "target":"es2021","module":"esnext","moduleResolution":"bundler","strict":true }
Dee: interesting. Overloads + conditional types can collapse into `unknown` when the bundler can't pick the right .d.ts path. Also note some packagers rewrite import specifiers which breaks type-only exports.
Aria: quick local workaround: switch to named import path that points directly at the esm build, e.g. `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference/esm'` (we should not encourage that long-term).
Noah: runtime mismatch often tracks back to default vs named interop from conditional exports. We should ensure exports map has explicit `import`/`require`/`node`/`edge` conditions and a `types` condition for edge consumers.
Ivy: another wrinkle: our tool outputs are union types with generics like `ToolResult<T> = { ok: true; payload: T } | { ok: false; error: string }`. TS loses the generic when the method is overloaded in a way that relies on type inference from call-site generics.
Dee: two options: (1) make the public API accept `unknown` and provide a `decodeTool<T>` helper so users opt in to decoding, or (2) expose a `StrictClient` type in a `@redwood/inference/strict` typing-only entry that preserves narrow unions and mapped types for TS strict users.
Aria: for onboarding friction, add `examples/ts/vite-edge` with a `tsconfig.edge.json` that shows `moduleResolution: node16` or `nodeNext` as alternatives, and a short README explaining why named imports are safer for some bundlers.
Noah: also surface in docs the `unknown vs any` tradeoff. For beginners, `any` makes quickstarts less noisy; for teams with strict CI we should document the `strict` typing import path.
Ivy: auth/retry note: in workers fetch rejects differently and AbortController quirks can convert errors to plain objects. Our retry wrapper assumes `err.code` patterns from Node. We should normalize error shape at the SDK boundary and avoid calling node-only methods like `.destroy()`.
Dee: good idea: add an `normalizeError(err)` util and run it in the top-level request pipeline so both edge and node see the same shape. Tests should include a mock worker environment.
types-bot: CI: examples/vite-edge types check failed on linux (ts 4.9 & 5.1 matrix) https://ci.internal/edge/999
Noah: action items: 
- Dee: prototype `normalizeError` and edge-safe retry guards (owner: Dee)
- Ivy: add example `examples/ts/vite-edge` + recommended tsconfigs and README (owner: Ivy)
- Aria: update package.json export map to include explicit `types` path and an `edge` condition (owner: Aria)
- Noah: draft typings proposal: ergonomic defaults + opt-in strict types entry and a migration guide for teams (owner: Noah)
Ivy: I'll drop a tiny repro and the tsconfigs in the example repo tonight. Tag me in #devex if you want early access. :seedling:
